evidence_quotes.quote: Since then SA has been successful in developing a household sanitation delivery model called ‘One Home-One Toilet’ (OHOT), which is scalable, replicable, and sustainable. It is unique because of its data-driven, community centric and cost sharing approach.

From June 2016 to June 2018, the impact assessment was carried out internally to determine the impact of SAs OHOT projects within four urban areas of Maharashtra: Kolhapur, Navi-Mumbai, Pimpri-Chinchwad, and Pune.

Our study reveals that 99% households have expressed their satisfaction about having chosen the OHOT model which is cost sharing model where the beneficiaries contribute financially as they bear the labour cost towards the toilet construction.

rationale: Full-text empirical paper evaluating Shelter Associates' 'One Home-One Toilet' (OHOT) urban slum sanitation model across four cities in Maharashtra (463 households surveyed pre- and post-intervention, six months apart). The intervention combines two co-central rule/delivery mechanisms: (1) NGO-led community mobilization, GIS mapping/ULB coordination, and women's sanitation committees (`participation_assistance`, primary framing mechanism), and (2) an explicit cost-sharing subsidy rule in which the NGO supplies construction materials in phases while beneficiary households bear labour and finishing costs (`fees_tariffs_subsidies`, empirically evaluated in Section 3). Outcomes span functional toilet usage replacing Community Toilet Blocks/open defecation and >6-month functionality (`effective_access`, primary pre-post outcome), physical household toilet installation inside small slum dwellings (`primary_connection`), and household cost-sharing expenditure (`economic_access`). The primary dataset analyzed in Tables 1-4 is an observational single-group pre-post household survey of 463 beneficiary families.
